races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 84 with a recent 5-day turnaround, confirmed front-runner who won over 5f Good on last outing; Denis Hogan's yard is hitting form (2/19 T14) and Chris Hayes is a strong booking, though a recent run record showing a 0 and an 8 suggests inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Daneh Of Dandy
runners_data.note: James Tate's 3yo returns after 62 days off but boasts strong 5f Good credentials including a win, and the fresh profile at a yard with a recent winner (1/13 T14) is a positive angle; settles in a prominent position naturally, which suits this race shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good and placed over 5f Good but is a genuine hold-up runner who needs the pace to fall apart in front — the fade-in-finish flag is a real concern in a race where the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to create a true late opportunity.

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: Dual 5f winner here at Down Royal with course form that is genuinely compelling, but her natural instinct to race prominently means she'll be crowded out of that position in this field and forced to race in unfamiliar midfield territory; the tongue-tie is noted and the style compromise is a significant headwind.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo for Gavin Cromwell stepping back to 5f from 6f, with placed efforts at both trips on Good ground; hood fitted, ran just 5 days ago, and Rory Mulligan is an experienced claiming rider — sits naturally in the prominent group that benefits from this race shape.

runners_data.name: Two And Two
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Sligo (Standard) and is a natural front-runner type who will find himself pushed back into midfield when Sarahmae asserts; the horse has no turf Good-ground form of note and is an apprentice-ridden 3yo dropping sharply in grade, but the style compromise is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Winless from four recent starts with a fade-in-finish flag, last ran 7 days ago, and the form string 0-0900 offers no encouragement; Shay Wallace takes the ride for a yard without a recent winner (0/13 T14) and the 5f trip looks sharp for a horse whose best turf form has been over longer.

races.paceDynamic: Sarahmae is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 5f on Good turf at Down Royal. Daneh Of Dandy and Treasured Royal will track in close attendance, creating an organised, strung-out early order rather than a contested burn-out. The field holds more prominent types than the front positions can accommodate — Mary Shoelaces and Two And Two are both natural prominent racers who will be squeezed back into a midfield role they do not naturally fill, which compromises their chances. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a measured pace with a tight cluster of prominent trackers — strongly favours horses that can sit just off the lead and pounce in the final furlong rather than true closers, who will find the pace insufficiently strong to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sarahmae Leads, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sarahmae dictates a controlled pace and the horses tracking in second and third positions have enough in reserve to challenge in the final 150 yards.
scenarios.body: If Sarahmae dictates a controlled pace and the horses tracking in second and third positions have enough in reserve to challenge in the final 150 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Sarahmae sets is genuinely modest and the field never quite gets close enough to reel her in.
scenarios.body: If the pace Sarahmae sets is genuinely modest and the field never quite gets close enough to reel her in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than anticipated and the front group ties up, leaving Shadow Of The Moon to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is stronger than anticipated and the front group ties up, leaving Shadow Of The Moon to close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Mary Shoelaces or Two And Two refuse to settle for their mapped midfield position and push forward to compete for prominent ground, injecting unexpected early pressure.
scenarios.body: If Mary Shoelaces or Two And Two refuse to settle for their mapped midfield position and push forward to compete for prominent ground, injecting unexpected early pressure.

watchPoints.text: Daneh Of Dandy — the 62-day break is the one question mark on the most naturally suited horse in the race; watch the market move to confirm trainer confidence, as a well-backed return would significantly shorten this profile's probability of landing Scenario A.

Mary Shoelaces — if she breaks sharply and manages to secure a prominent position despite the traffic, the course-winning form at Down Royal over 5f Good makes her a live danger; watch how she loads and exits the stalls.

Two And Two — similarly, any aggressive early move by Conor Cusack to push for the front could compress the early pace and unsettle Sarahmae's rhythm, triggering Scenario D; monitor early positioning in the first furlong.

Sarahmae — ran just 5 days ago and the recent form shows a bounce-back win sandwiched between defeats; if she shows any sign of reluctance to stride on from the front, the race shape collapses and the prominent trackers inherit the advantage immediately.

Shadow Of The Moon — Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is useful but the fade-in-finish flag over a trip that already tests staying power means this runner is worth watching only if the early pace is unexpectedly strong; in a controlled-pace scenario she is likely to come up short.

races.name: WillWeGo Handicap

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who shapes as the sole pace-setter here; her sim-going record on good turf is thin (0 wins, 0 places in 2 runs) and she is racing out of her natural prominent tag into a lead role — discount the raw OR-69 at face value and focus on whether she can control without burning out.

runners_data.name: Aughlish
runners_data.note: Most authentic hold-up runner in the field with a clean 5f record at Slane and Leopardstown; blinkers on today sharpens her for the dash and, given she is the only uncontested closer, any clear run in the final furlong makes her a live threat at OR-68.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground on his most recent start and handles this trip and going combination well; sits prominently and his sim-going record (1W, 1P from 4 runs) is the strongest in the field on comparable conditions — clean passage from a tracking position is all he needs.

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: 191 days off the track is a significant fitness concern for a lightly-raced two-year-old turning three; seven runs on good or good-to-firm ground give him the going profile, and he posted four places from eight sim-going starts, but the absence is impossible to ignore.

runners_data.name: This Guy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has contested 5f good-ground races recently with modest success (best effort a fourth); headgear including a tongue-tie has been tried and he tends to plug on without threatening — needs a messy race to capitalise.

runners_data.name: Baby Basma
runners_data.note: Has a course-equivalent win on good going over 5f which is an important credential in this field; 57 days between runs and a hood worn today suggest connections are managing her carefully — Leigh Roche knows her from that winning run and she is live if fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Ran second over 5f on good ground in her most recent sim-going appearance — that is genuinely encouraging — but her natural hold-up style means she is pushed into midfield by the congestion of closers, and getting to the front from that compressed position is a tall ask on this sharp track.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: Six consecutive zeros in the form string tell a bleak story; trainer-jockey combination with zero wins from 14-day records and a crowded field where the true hold-up role she is mapped away from only adds further complication — hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Trainer Michael Mulvany has sent three winners from 16 runners in the past 14 days which is a strong yard stat; Mini Cotai herself wears hood and has reasonable 5f good-ground form, but her true hold-up style is mapped into midfield by the surplus of closers — watch the yard angle but note the positional compromise.

races.paceDynamic: Gonna Be Golden is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing or able to dispute the lead, she should control tempo from the gates on good ground over five furlongs at Down Royal. Cashel Blue and The Right One are both prominent-style runners who will look to sit close to the pace, but neither has the profile to force the issue and turn this into a true test. That uncontested lead creates a sustainable, gallop that will reward horses who can track in behind and produce a clean run in the final furlong, suiting prominent-to-midfield profiles who don't have to cover excessive ground. Spirit Above, The Love Machine, and Mini Cotai are true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield solely because there is a surplus of closers in this field — in practice, they are unlikely to get a clean run from where they will actually be racing, which tilts the shape further toward the prominent tracking position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden Controls, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gonna Be Golden leads without pressure and sets a honest but manageable tempo, horses who sit second or third in the slipstream land in the ideal position.
scenarios.body: If Gonna Be Golden leads without pressure and sets a honest but manageable tempo, horses who sit second or third in the slipstream land in the ideal position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Gonna Be Golden bowls along comfortably enough to never be headed, she steals the race rather than surrendering it.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow and Gonna Be Golden bowls along comfortably enough to never be headed, she steals the race rather than surrendering it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and Gonna Be Golden sets a strong gallop, hold-up horses find daylight in the final stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected and Gonna Be Golden sets a strong gallop, hold-up horses find daylight in the final stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Breaks Out
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and traffic issues disrupt the midfield contingent, a horse who finds an unexpected clear passage steals the race from an unfancied position.
scenarios.body: If the field bunches and traffic issues disrupt the midfield contingent, a horse who finds an unexpected clear passage steals the race from an unfancied position.

watchPoints.text: Cashel Blue's recent win on good ground over 5f is the standout form line — watch whether he can secure a clean prominent position behind Gonna Be Golden from the gates, as that is the race-winning spot.

Spirit Above, The Love Machine, and Mini Cotai are all genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield — monitor the early stages for a bunched, congested pack that could cost several of them a clear run turning for home.
The Right One's 191-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race; watch the market moves and paddock demeanour for signs she is ready to do herself justice first time back.

Baby Basma runs with a hood today having been off 57 days — if she shows any signs of freshness in the preliminary ring that could be a positive fitness signal for a horse who won on comparable good ground.

Gonna Be Golden's price in running will be instructive — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged through the first two furlongs, the pace dynamic solidifies firmly around Scenario A and the trackers behind her become the primary focus.

races.name: Ampion Electrical Test And Solar Handicap

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, likely to lead unopposed on his terms; Good-ground form is modest (2/15 in similar conditions, 0 wins), and the drop to 5f from his recent 6f starts is worth noting, but controlling the pace is a significant natural advantage here.

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Excellent 5f Good-ground record (2 wins, 3 places from 8 runs in similar conditions) makes him the standout on applicable form; hold-up style means Donagh O'Connor will need to be patient, but this trip and going combination suits him better than almost anyone in the field.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old prominent racer with Edward Lynam, who has gone 0/5 in the last 14 days; placed at 5f on Soft/Standard but his Good-ground record here is limited — will try to sit second and grind.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a hold-up type who has placed three times at 5f on Good but also registered a 16th-place finish at this trip recently; blinkers applied, but her recent form string (30-200) is deeply discouraging and confidence in her finishing strongly is low.

runners_data.name: Jordan Breeze
runners_data.note: Apprentice Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (7lb claim) aboard a 4-year-old prominent racer who has placed twice at 5f on Standard; his best form came on Soft and figures to be just adequate rather than competitive on Good ground here.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Shay Wallace (7lb claim) rides a 6-year-old who has run 12 of 15 career efforts in similar going conditions — among the most course/ground-experienced in the field at 5-6f; ran 2nd and 3rd at 5f Good recently and his prominent style suits the anticipated race shape well.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) partners a filly who has run only once on Good going (17th at 6f) and is stepping back from 6-7f; trainer Harry Cleaary has had no runners in the last 14 days, which adds a layer of uncertainty, and her overall profile looks light for this company.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Jack Kearney (3lb claim) rides a genuine hold-up horse — a winner at 6f Good — who has been mapped closer to midfield simply because the field is stacked with closers; the tongue-tie is retained, but being unable to fully settle at the rear is a real tactical cost given his natural racing style.

runners_data.name: Verified
runners_data.note: Carries a finishing-fade flag and his last three runs on Good going placed him 17th, 10th, and 12th; Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) has him repositioned closer than ideal to his true rear-of-field preference, and the weight of evidence on this surface and in this shape is heavily against him.

runners_data.name: She's A Gift
runners_data.note: Conor Cusack (7lb claim) rides a filly whose best form reads 2nd at 5f on Standard; she's a natural hold-up type whose most recent Good-ground run produced a 14th-place finish, and being unable to operate from her preferred position at the back further limits her prospects.

runners_data.name: Skillman Ave
runners_data.note: Carries a finishing-fade flag alongside an 8th-place finish at 5f Good in recent history; Jessica Maye (7lb claim) partners a hold-up mare wearing a hood who has never won beyond a single victory, and her inability to drop in naturally to the rear on a compact 5f course makes her tactical situation especially awkward.

races.paceDynamic: Clonmacash is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f handicap on Good ground at Down Royal, and with no genuine rival to press him from the outside, he is set to control affairs from the gates and dictate a sustainable, measured tempo rather than a barn-burner. Collective Power and Jordan Breeze will attempt to race prominently just off his flank, while Nouvel Espoir — with excellent course-form indicators — will also push forward and keep Clonmacash honest without necessarily forcing him into a truly punishing gallop. With the pace single-sourced and the ground riding consistently Good across the card, this shape strongly favours horses able to race in the top half of the field, tracking a controlled pace and staying on through the final furlong rather than closing from deep. This field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Spirit Of Eagles, Verified, She's A Gift, and Skillman Ave are all genuine closers who are likely to find themselves nearer midfield than their preferred ground, compromising their ability to produce a true late charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clonmacash Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Clonmacash leads uncontested at a sustainable clip and the pace is not forced high by the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: If Clonmacash leads uncontested at a sustainable clip and the pace is not forced high by the chasing pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Take Over
scenarios.trigger: If Clonmacash fades inside the final furlong and those sitting second or third sweep through to claim the prize.
scenarios.body: If Clonmacash fades inside the final furlong and those sitting second or third sweep through to claim the prize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected, the front rank ties up, and one of the hold-up horses finds a gap late.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected, the front rank ties up, and one of the hold-up horses finds a gap late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Breaks Out Early
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types contest the early lead aggressively, the pace fractures and leaves a wide-open final furlong.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types contest the early lead aggressively, the pace fractures and leaves a wide-open final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Clonmacash has no pace rival to challenge him early — watch whether Sam Coen (5lb claim) allows him to dictate a very comfortable lead, as any slow early pace could allow closer types to close ground they would not normally make on a true 5f Good track.

Arctic Steps is the most dangerous closer in the field on 5f Good form, but Donagh O'Connor must work efficiently from a hold-up position with a field full of similarly-styled horses — watch for traffic issues in the final two furlongs if the race tightens up.

Nouvel Espoir has run 12 times in similar going and has the Shay Wallace 7lb claim on board — watch his market moves pre-race as his genuine Good-ground record and prominent style make him a quiet live runner if his odds drift into value territory.

Four redistributed hold-up horses (Spirit Of Eagles, Verified, She's A Gift, Skillman Ave) will be racing closer than their natural style dictates — watch for congestion and bump-and-shuffle in the midfield pack from the 2f pole inward, which could affect clean runs for multiple runners simultaneously.

The Good ground has been consistent across all seven races on the card — no variance expected — but watch for any dramatic drying if the evening sun strengthens, as Clonmacash's heavy-ground (hg:v) flag suggests he may actually be flattered by the current conditions.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Proparamedics And Medicall Handicap

runners_data.name: Royal Saxo
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here and likely to dictate from the outset; A J Martin yard out of form (0/8 in 14 days) and recent form shows a drop back from 10f trips, which is a concern, but the ability to control fractions from stall adds significant tactical value.

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Standside going and drops back to 7f here; true hold-up style should see him race at the rear, and his 40-day absence is worth noting, but the drop in trip adds a finishing kick dimension if the pace is strong enough.

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over 7f including a second last time out; naturally prominent and well-suited to tracking Royal Saxo, though only 1 win from 15 similar-going starts tempers expectations and the claim-riding apprentice is notable.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has found 7f on Good ground workable (placed last time out); McGuinness yard is busy but out of form (0/25 in 14 days), and this horse has not won in recent outings on this surface type.

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: True hold-up racer with a patchy recent record including a 13th last time out on Good; hood fitted and a 26-day break, but recent form figures make it hard to make a strong case on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Prominent style with a third at 8f on Good ground recently; McGuinness runner alongside Flaming Rib and the yard's 14-day record (0/25) is a drag, though a return to 7f and Good ground matches his better historical efforts.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: Won over 7f Good and placed over 8f Good recently; Chris Hayes in the saddle adds riding quality, and a naturally prominent style means he can slot in just behind Royal Saxo without burning fuel — well-suited to the expected shape.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: Exceptional form profile for this ground — all nine recent runs on Good, including six placed efforts and four seconds; J P Murtagh yard in form (4/35 in 14 days), prominent style fits the race shape, and the consistent placed record makes her a key player.

runners_data.name: Thurso
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Firm recently and steps up to 7f; prominent profile suits tracking the leader, and two wins from four Good-ground runs historically is encouraging, though stepping up in trip for the first time in a while is a small unknown.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who is redistributed to the midfield map position given the volume of hold-up runners in this field; Patrick Flynn yard placed one winner in 14 days, and recent form shows a 0-0 in last two runs, making it hard to build a strong case.

runners_data.name: Battle Borne
runners_data.note: Raced just yesterday (1-day turnaround) which is an immediate concern; genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, and recent form figures (zeros) give little encouragement regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is pushed into a midfield position on the map because the prominent berths are oversubscribed; dropping back from 10f trips to 7f is a significant question, and the style-fit discount applies given the likely inability to secure a forward position.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: McGuinness's third runner in the race and the yard's 14-day stats are poor; prefers to race prominently but is unlikely to secure that berth with so many rivals ahead of him, running in hood and tongue-tie, and recent form figures (0-7-3-5-6-5) suggest modest current ability.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Saxo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 7f handicap at Down Royal, and with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, he is set to control proceedings at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good turf. Behind him, Little Empire, Summer Island, Treasure Rose, Eddie G, and Thurso all carry prominent profiles and will compete for the early positions just off the pace, creating a reasonably organised but potentially crowded middle section. The field does contain more pace than the map can fully accommodate — Gotta Catch'em All and Minaun View are genuine prominent types who are likely to find themselves racing in midfield rather than their natural position, and both carry a style-fit discount as a result. With a single leader setting a sustainable rhythm and no pressure forcing a truly honest gallop, this race shape favours prominent racers who can travel just behind Royal Saxo and produce a clean, well-timed challenge from a handy position without burning energy fighting for early ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Saxo dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and his rivals are unable to close the gap from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Royal Saxo dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and his rivals are unable to close the gap from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Saxo sets an honest gallop and one or two prominent trackers produce a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Royal Saxo sets an honest gallop and one or two prominent trackers produce a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace accelerates sharply mid-race, stringing the field out and creating conditions for a strong late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace accelerates sharply mid-race, stringing the field out and creating conditions for a strong late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group sets a contested early fractions and the field bunches, causing a tactical scramble late.
scenarios.body: If the crowded prominent group sets a contested early fractions and the field bunches, causing a tactical scramble late.

watchPoints.text: Royal Saxo's ability to control fractions entirely unopposed is the single biggest shape factor — if any of the crowded prominent group (Little Empire, Summer Island, Treasure Rose) pushes up to challenge early, the pace lifts and the race opens up for hold-up horses.

Treasure Rose has six recent placed efforts on Good ground and is course-proven at this distance; her consistency means she is a constant threat to any prominent runner who does not sustain their effort, and she must be covered at all times late.

Gotta Catch'em All and Minaun View are natural prominent types who may attempt to force their way forward from wide draws despite the map position — if both push up aggressively, the early pace could spike unexpectedly and unsettle the anticipated controlled shape.
Battle Borne raced yesterday and the 1-day turnaround at Down Royal on Good ground is a stamina and freshness concern — monitor in the parade ring and factor into any hold-up scenario assessment.

The McGuinness trio (Flaming Rib, Eddie G, Minaun View) running together creates potential for a tactical team move; watch for any of the three being ridden with unusual urgency early, which could signal a deliberate pace injection from the yard.

races.name: Laura Nicholas Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a recent record that includes a third and a fifth over 7f on Good ground at similar tracks; OR 60 gives weight concessions over several rivals and Scott McCullagh is effective from handy positions, but the form string shows inconsistency and a win from this high draw (if wide) would require Dervo Annie to fold.|

runners_data.name: Alex Belardo
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer whose recent form has been entirely on slow ground at Dundalk, posting a string of close finishes in that format; similar-going figures are weak (2/15) on turf, and the step to genuine Good at Down Royal at 7f may expose a surface limitation.|

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with limited turf-on-Good form (5/15 similar-going), last seen unplaced at 11th over 7f on Good; the 46-day absence needs monitoring and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/3 does little to build confidence on this return.|

runners_data.name: Hot To Foxtrot
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed third over 6f on Good last time and has three placings from nine similar-going runs; Wesley Joyce holds the 3lb apprentice claim and this horse's consistent proximity to pace makes it a genuine player if the gallop stays steady.|

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from a 126-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — and has not shown ability on Good ground (0 wins, 0 places from 5 similar-going runs); the extended break is the key risk factor here.|

runners_data.name: Ukiyo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 11 runs on similar going, posting a win and three placings; placed second over 7f on Good and second over 6f on Heavy, indicating versatility, and the 7-day turnaround suggests the trainer Andrew Kinirons is happy with the horse's condition.|

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer by record, but the field's density of hold-up types means it is unlikely to race from its preferred position; placed 4th on Good over 8f but all recent form is on Tapeta or Heavy going, and the blinkers on for the first time adds uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, and she has already won over 6f on Good and placed second over 7f on Good this season, confirming her effectiveness at this track and surface; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is a tangible advantage and she only needs to find the front without being immediately pressed to control the tempo.|

runners_data.name: Concaire
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed second over 7f on Good at Navan earlier this season; Chris Hayes is one of the stronger jockeys in the field and knows how to position off a moderate pace, giving this horse a legitimate tactical option if it gets a handy berth.|

runners_data.name: Zephron
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old whose recent form on Good includes a placing at 7th but who carries the fade-in-finish flag; shown to struggle over this distance on similar going (7/15 similar-going) and, as a true hold-up type forced into a midfield position, the tactical situation is against it.|

runners_data.name: Lady Kelly
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with a fade-in-finish flag and just one run on Good going in her last four, finishing sixth over 7f; the 3-year-old is lightly-raced with a short form history, and Yudish Geerdharry's 7lb claim on a filly with limited experience is a double-edged factor.|

runners_data.name: Miqdaad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse whose recent form on Good includes a second and several midfield finishes; as a natural hold-up type facing redistribution into midfield, it is unlikely to race from its favoured position, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the risk in a race with a pedestrian pace.|

runners_data.name: Rock Etoile
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with three-placing on Good going (3rd over 8f Good recently) who is genuinely suited to hold-up tactics, yet the redistribution issue means finding a position further back than ideal will be difficult; fade-in-finish flag and a 7lb apprentice rider are notable negatives.|

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type with tongue-tie and pads in headgear; the 39-day break after a fourth-place finish on Good is workable, but as a horse whose recent wins have all come at Dundalk on standard (7 similar-going runs, 0 wins on turf), the switch back to Good turf for a third time without success is a telling pattern.|

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with four runs on Good going, all returning positions of 6th, 12th, 8th and 15th; the fade-in-finish flag and a form string that reads 0809-6 suggests this horse has never threatened competitively on turf, and racing out of its natural hold-up position will not improve matters.|

runners_data.name: Royal County Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who won over 7f on Standard and placed third over 6f on Standard; only 3 similar-going runs on turf but does have form figures on Good (9th and 5th), and at OR 60 this 3-year-old is well-treated if it secures a true rearward position and the pace develops.|

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran aged 10 with a win and two placings on similar Good ground (6/8f, 9/15 similar-going); tongue-tie and blinkers suggest a trainer trying to get the best from him late in his career, and genuine hold-up runs at 5th over 8f and 2nd over 8f on Good in his last three keep him relevant if a true end-to-end gallop develops.|

races.paceDynamic: Dervo Annie is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one pace-setter in a 17-runner field at 7f on Good turf, she is poised to control this race at a measured, sustainable gallop from the outset. Blue Anthem, Hot To Foxtrot, Ukiyo, Pete's Dream and Concaire will press for prominent berths just off the leader, meaning the opening quarter-mile will see a busy shake-out for position before the pace settles. The single-pace dynamic and absence of a true pace battle means the race is unlikely to produce a genuinely end-to-end test; instead a moderate tempo with a mid-race lull is the most probable shape, leaving plenty in the tank for those racing close to the action turning for home. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers and handy types who can travel within striking distance of the steady pace and produce a strong finishing effort over the final two furlongs — hold-up horses face a structurally disadvantaged task because they will need the pace to collapse ahead of them, which a lone front-runner rarely delivers. The field also holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Toy Soldier, Stonyfalls, Zephron, Mullacash Buzz, Rock Etoile and Miqdaad are all true hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled forward out of their natural position, with only Lady Kelly, Royal County Glory and Brains likely to secure authentic rearward berths.

watchPoints.text: Dervo Annie is the only confirmed front-runner — watch whether she is allowed to stride straight to the lead unchallenged in the first furlong, because an uncontested lead on Good ground over 7f makes her the key race-shaper and potential winner.

Blue Anthem, Hot To Foxtrot and Ukiyo will all compete for the same handy position just off the leader; if two or three clash for second berth in the early stages, the resulting friction could inject unexpected pace and compromise each other's finishing effort.

Toy Soldier, Zephron, Mullacash Buzz, Rock Etoile and Miqdaad are all genuine hold-up horses who cannot all race from the rear in a 17-runner field — watch for traffic issues and positional chaos in the first two furlongs as these horses struggle to find their preferred spot.

Ukiyo runs just 7 days after its last start and has placed on Good ground over both 6f and 7f; watch how sharply it travels in the first three furlongs as a guide to whether the quick turnaround has left it fresh or flat.

Royal County Glory and Brains are the two hold-up horses most likely to secure authentic rearward berths; watch how much ground they have to make up at the 2f pole — if they are within three lengths of the leaders at that point, the steady pace may have left the door open.
